sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Orland Park, Illinois?
sections.html:
Orland Park sellers have three practical routes: a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, or a direct cash purchase. A cash buyer can close the fastest, while a listing often brings the highest price for a house in good order.

Orland Park is a village of about 22 square miles 25 miles southwest of Chicago, and most of it lies in Cook County with a small piece in Will County. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 57,954 residents, and 24.8% of them are 65 or older.

  • List with an agent when the roof, furnace and kitchen are in decent shape and you can wait through showings and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • Sell it yourself when you are comfortable negotiating and coordinating with a title company and the village.
  • Take a cash offer when the house needs repairs, a probate is pending, or a tenant must be dealt with. Compare it against a listing price less commission, repairs and months of carrying costs.

sections.h2: How did Orland Park grow into the village it is today?
sections.html:
Orland Park began as a farming settlement called Orland in 1834 and grew into a large suburb mainly after 1960. The village was incorporated on May 31, 1892, after a Wabash Railroad line built in 1879 brought the town its first station, Sedgwick Station.

The population counts show how late the growth came: 788 in 1950, 2,592 in 1960, 23,045 in 1980, 51,077 in 2000 and 58,703 in 2020. Orland Square Mall opened in 1976, and shopping centers such as Orland Park Crossing followed. Most of the village's present population arrived after 1960.

The village likes to call itself the World's Golf Center. Village lore says someone counted 1,089 golf holes within 15 miles, and the slogan is painted on seven water towers. Wikipedia also notes planned downtown redevelopment at 143rd Street and LaGrange Road, the Main Street Triangle, with an estimated completion in fall 2027.

sections.h2: What roads and trains connect Orland Park to Chicago?
sections.html:
Interstate 80 forms the southern edge of the village, and Metra's SouthWest Service stops at 143rd Street, 153rd Street and 179th Street. Those three stations give commuters train service to Chicago Union Station on weekdays, with Pace buses on several routes.

The main corridors for drivers are La Grange Road (U.S. 45) north to south, 159th Street (U.S. 6) east to west, Harlem Avenue (Illinois 43) near the eastern border, Illinois 7, and 167th Street, which runs entirely inside the village. For 2020-2024 the Census Bureau reports a 33.8-minute average commute.

Orland Park's neighbors are Homer Glen to the west, Orland Hills and Mokena to the south, Tinley Park to the southeast, Oak Forest to the east, and Palos Park and Palos Heights to the north. Two bodies of water, Lake Sedgwick and McGinnis Slough, lie inside the village limits.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Orland Park addresses?
sections.html:
Most of the Cook County part of Orland Park is in Orland School District 135, and all of it feeds Consolidated High School District 230, whose Carl Sandburg High School serves most of the village. Addresses in the northern edge may instead be zoned to Stagg or Victor J. Andrew high schools, so confirm the exact school for your street.

Four elementary districts reach Orland Park in Cook County: District 135, Community Consolidated District 146, Palos District 118 and Kirby District 140. District 135 runs Century, Jerling and Orland junior highs. In Will County, Mokena School District 159 and Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210 cover homes in the village. St. Michael School is the Archdiocese of Chicago school in the village, and Moraine Valley Community College in nearby Palos Hills offers community college classes.

sections.h2: What local amenities do buyers ask about in Orland Park?
sections.html:
Buyers mostly ask about parks, shopping and the village's recreation facilities, and Orland Park has plenty of each. The village lists more than 60 parks, and Centennial Park holds the Aquatic Center with six water slides, Lake Sedgwick with boardwalks and pedal boats, and a free outdoor ice rink that runs from November to March.

The Sportsplex on 159th Street is the largest indoor recreation building, with three basketball courts, an indoor soccer field and a quarter-mile track. Shopping centers include Orland Square Mall and Orland Park Crossing, and healthcare, finance and retail make up much of the local employment base. The Taste of Orland Park food festival is held at the Village Center in early August, and the village hosts Independence Day fireworks in Centennial Park West.

Census data show a settled community: 90.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 25.9% of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home. A listing that names the nearest park, Metra station and school boundary answers the questions buyers raise first.

sections.h2: Does Orland Park require anything from a seller or a landlord?
sections.html:
The village runs a rental registration program, and it applies to single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums as well as apartment buildings. The annual fee is $100 per unit for a detached or attached single-family residence and $100 plus $15 per additional unit for a multi-family building.

  • Inspections follow the village's tri-annual schedule, and a rental housing sticker is issued when the unit passes.
  • Landlords or their agents must attend one eight-hour Crime Free Housing seminar from the police department.
  • Every lease must carry the village's Crime Free Lease Addendum, signed by each tenant age 18 or older.

When a rental is part of the sale, tell the buyer whether the unit is registered and when the last inspection took place. Development Services answers registration questions at (708) 403-5300.

sections.h2: How do I handle water service and county taxes when selling in Orland Park?
sections.html:
Water is billed every two months by the village, and a high bill should be reviewed by calling 708-403-6175. Property owners are responsible for the private water line from the shut-off valve, usually in the parkway, to the house, plus any leaks inside.

Property tax comes from Cook County. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 reassessment group, and the township assessor's office is at 14807 S. Ravinia Ave., phone (708) 403-4222. For tax year 2025 the Cook County Treasurer set the first installment due date at April 1, 2026 and the second at October 1, 2026, and both have passed. Ask the Treasurer for the next due date and ask your closing agent how the year's tax is prorated between you and the buyer.

A small part of Orland Park lies in Will County. If your house is in that part, ask the Will County treasurer for the schedule on your bill.

faqs.q: Does Orland Park charge a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the village finance office and your title company which village charges apply to your closing, and get the figures in writing before the closing date.

faqs.q: Which county bills property tax in Orland Park?
faqs.a: Cook County, for almost all of the village. A small part sits in Will County and is billed there. Check the first digits and the county named on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Orland Park before selling it?
faqs.a: If it is rented, yes, the village requires annual registration at $100 per unit for a single-family home, with inspections on a tri-annual schedule. Share the registration and inspection records with the buyer.

faqs.q: Where do I report a high final water bill in Orland Park?
faqs.a: Call the village water billing line at 708-403-6175. The village bills two months at a time, and owners are responsible for leaks on the private line and inside the house.

faqs.q: How is Orland Park's reassessment schedule set?
faqs.a: Cook County reassesses each township every three years. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 group, so a new notice arrives in the reassessment year and the township assessor can answer questions.
